mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for 4 consecutive months reduces expected discount rates, lowering the present value of future equity cash flows and thus producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the policy tightening phase, with p-value > 0.05 in a two-sample test against pre-tightening periods.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months, labor market strength is interpreted as supporting corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0 and UNRATE remains below for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the prior 60-day average during similar labor market conditions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the HOUST index (household spending) by at least 3% in a single month is associated with increased consumer confidence and higher expected corporate profits, yielding positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥3% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat during periods of strong HOUST growth (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 5% over three months indicates supply-side contraction, which raises uncertainty and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥5% over three consecutive months
failure_condition: During supply contraction, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in CPIAUCSL of 0.3% or more signal accelerating inflation, prompting the Fed to maintain higher rates, which depresses equity discount rates and yields negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥0.3% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during periods of CPIAUCSL declines (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in PAYEMS (employment months) exceeding 200,000 in a month indicates strong labor absorption, which is associated with corporate optimism and positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the prior 60-day average during similar labor absorption events (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE (federal funds rate rise coupled with labor market weakening) creates a dual pressure on discounting and earnings expectations, resulting in negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases and UNRATE decreases over the same horizon
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when both proxies move in the opposite direction (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a post-crisis recovery regime (defined by HOUST > 1100 and UNRATE < 5%), S&P 20-day forward returns are consistently positive due to optimism about economic resilience.
candidate_trigger: regime condition: HOUST > 1100 and UNRATE < 5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In the defined regime, 20-day forward returns are not positive (mean ≤ 0) or the regime persists for <3 months (p > 0.05).
